framework: Japan - Digital Agency DS-920 Guideline for Japanese Government's Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI, v2.0 (decided 12 Jun 2026; in force 1 Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: CAIOs shall conduct risk assessments at project planning and, for generative AI systems likely to be high-risk, report project details, objectives, risk mitigation measures and quality assurance plans (including during operation) to the Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board; reporting also applies at development, release and post-launch if high-risk status arises; CAIOs report a status list about quarterly.
what_is_tested: Reporting of risk assessment, mitigation and quality assurance plans for likely high-risk generative AI
who_tests: CAIO reports to Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board
language_read: English provisional translation (Digital Agency) checked against Japanese original

framework: Japan - Digital Agency DS-920 Guideline for Japanese Government's Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI, v2.0 (decided 12 Jun 2026; in force 1 Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: The v2.0 decision takes effect on 1 Sep 2026; CAIO measures under Sec. 6.2 were to be set by 30 Jun 2026 and the AI governance framework scope under Sec. 2.2.2 applies from 1 Jul 2026.
what_is_tested: Not applicable
language_read: English provisional translation (Digital Agency) checked against Japanese original

framework: South Korea - Enforcement Decree of the AI Framework Act (Presidential Decree No. 36053, 21 Jan 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: The impact assessment of high-impact AI must cover: affected persons/groups; affected fundamental rights; content and scope of social and economic impacts; usage patterns; quantitative and qualitative metrics and methods used; measures to prevent and mitigate risks and recover losses; and, where needed, an improvement plan. The operator may conduct it itself or commission a third party; the Minister notifies other matters.
what_is_tested: Fundamental rights impact assessment content and method
language_read: English translation by KLRI (site states English version is for reference only, no legal effect)

framework: South Korea - Enforcement Decree of the AI Framework Act (Presidential Decree No. 36053, 21 Jan 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: An operator requesting MSIT confirmation of whether its AI is high-impact files the Appendix form with a product/service overview, training data overview, materials verifying the AI's process and results, and other documents; MSIT decides on criteria including use area, impact/severity/frequency of risks to life, safety and rights, and the operator's prior review; response within 30 days (extendable once by 30 days); reconfirmation request within 10 days, answered within 30 days after consulting the specialised committee.
what_is_tested: High-impact classification (pre-deployment confirmation on request)
who_tests: Operator submits; MSIT decides with specialised committee
language_read: English translation by KLRI (site states English version is for reference only, no legal effect)

framework: NCA 'Draft of AI Cybersecurity Guidelines' (AICG-1:2026), draft for public consultation (closed 5 Aug 2026)

framework: NCA 'Draft of AI Cybersecurity Guidelines' (AICG-1:2026), draft for public consultation (closed 5 Aug 2026)

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: For MDMA the manufacturer is expected to provide technical documentation including product verification and validation; documentation should show verification against design specifications, validation that the device performs as intended, a usability study, and validation of safe performance under normal and reasonably foreseeable abnormal conditions.
what_is_tested: Design conformance, intended performance, usability, behaviour under abnormal inputs
language_read: English official

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Manufacturers need to show valid clinical association, analytical/technical validation and clinical validation; clinical validation follows analytical validation, applies to all risk classes, and is evaluated before market placement and after; example metrics include sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV.
what_is_tested: Clinical association, analytical and clinical validity
language_read: English official

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Where independent review is needed, the clinical evaluation should as far as possible be reviewed by someone not significantly involved in development and with nothing to gain, proportionate to risk; an evaluation based on a comparator device must show clinical and technical equivalence including the algorithm.
what_is_tested: Independence of clinical evaluation review; equivalence claims
language_read: English official

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Analytical validation should use a large independent reference dataset reflecting the intended population (prevalence, multi-centre sourcing, demographics, justified size, not publicly available); performance should be shown to generalise through multisite investigation and subgroup analysis, and be tested against a gold standard.
what_is_tested: Generalisability, subgroup performance, test-data independence
language_read: English official

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Effects should be evaluated in clinically relevant conditions integrated into the clinical workflow, comparing clinicians with and without the device; manufacturers should locally validate devices developed and approved in other jurisdictions.
what_is_tested: Real-world clinical effect; local validity in KSA
language_read: English official

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Because AI/ML devices can learn continuously, manufacturers are required to use post-market continuous monitoring of safety, effectiveness and performance in real-world settings.
what_is_tested: Real-world safety, effectiveness and performance
language_read: English official

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Manufacturers are required (per MDS-REQ 1) to show no unacceptable risk and that benefits outweigh residual risk; safety requirements should include evaluation results on algorithm limitations and performance; a risk management review per ISO 14971:2019 Clause 9 should be performed before commercial release.
what_is_tested: Residual risk, algorithm limitations
language_read: English official

framework: SFDA MDS-G010 Guidance on AI and ML technologies based Medical Devices (v1.0, 29/11/2022)
requirement_paraphrase: SFDA is to be informed via GHAD of significant changes within 10 days; the manufacturer shall have QMS procedures for change control, and all changes shall be evaluated, verified and validated under those procedures.
what_is_tested: Verification and validation of device changes
language_read: English official

framework: SDAIA AI Service Provider Accreditation (National Data Governance Platform service)
requirement_paraphrase: AI software and service providers register, appoint an AI officer, and complete a per-product questionnaire with supporting files on adherence to AI ethics standards; after committee review the product receives an incentive label and the provider an accreditation certificate.
what_is_tested: Product-level adherence to AI ethics standards (questionnaire and files)
language_read: Arabic original (fetch-tool rendering)

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Self-Assessment tool (National Data Governance Platform service)
requirement_paraphrase: Tool for entities to compare their current practice against defined standards and obtain the level of ethical compliance of an AI model; links to the AI Ethics Principles.
what_is_tested: Ethical compliance level of an AI model
language_read: Arabic original (fetch-tool rendering)

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
clause_or_page: Overview (unnumbered, before p.2) of the PDF; mapping, date and audiences from the web page https://aiverifyfoundation.sg/tools/ai-verify-testing-framework/
requirement_paraphrase: Process-check framework to assess AI systems against 11 principles (transparency, explainability, reproducibility, safety, security, robustness, fairness, data governance, accountability, human agency and oversight, inclusive growth); each item has outcome, process and evidence, answered Yes/No/N/A with elaboration; mapped to NIST AI RMF, NIST GenAI Profile, Hiroshima Process code of conduct and ISO/IEC 42001.
what_is_tested: Responsible-AI process checks and technical tests
who_tests: AI system owner (self-assessment); internal compliance; external auditors may validate

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (version read: v1.0, 22 Jan 2026; v1.5 not read)
requirement_paraphrase: Test agents for safety and security before deployment, covering overall task execution, policy compliance (including routing for human approval), tool calling (right tool, permissions, inputs, order) and robustness to errors and edge cases; test entire workflows including reasoning and tool calls, and multi-agent systems.
what_is_tested: Agent behaviour across the whole workflow, tool use, multi-agent emergent behaviour
